name: Talos Machine Sensor 0.8.4 observer mode candidate
body: USB candidate for M5StickS3 from Talos source commit 508cffce9. One image with four runtime modes: octopus (machine counter), kvm (USB keyboard/mouse), humidity (Grove ENV probe) and observer (Pi Observer operator screen; same observer_state/observer_button USB contract as the old display-only build). Modes switch over USB serial device_mode_set, MQTT device_mode_set, device REST POST /config/device-mode, and MCP talos_iot_device_mode_set. kvm is never armed remotely; the physical button still arms input. Pair with tedge v0.2.18+ for 'tedge sensor flash-github'. Flash the complete image at 0x0, or bootloader/partitions/boot_app0/firmware at partition offsets from partitions.csv (otadata 0x69000, app0 0x70000). Checksummed but unsigned: not for automatic OTA or fleet rollout.

name: Talos Machine Sensor 0.8.2 hardware KVM candidate
body: Guarded USB candidate for M5StickS3 from Talos source commit 191e415fa. Adds device-acknowledged HID (status echoes lastHidCommandId/lastHidAccepted, capability talos.hardware-kvm.ack.v1; tedge reports E_KVM_DEVICE_REJECTED / E_KVM_NO_ACK instead of a blind ok), modifier-first key reports with 15 ms key-down for Delphi/VCL apps such as Logo, and the absolute-pointer warp fix. Pair with tedge v0.2.17. Flash over USB with edge/m5stick-sensor/scripts/flash-usb.sh --mode keyboard or tedge sensor flash (complete image at offset 0x0, partition offsets from partitions.csv). Checksummed but unsigned: not approved for automatic OTA or fleet rollout until the physical Pi + HDMI capture + StickS3 gates pass.

name: Talos Machine Sensor 0.7.2 power-source status canary
body:
Manual USB canary release for M5StickS3/K150.

- Adds a live top-right counter-screen badge: EXT for USB-C/power-bank input, BAT for internal battery.
- Exposes the same power-source state through safe serial diagnostics.
- Enforces always-on application operation for power-bank deployments.
- Supports solo and V0 cable operation; V1 PCB transport remains fail-closed and unreleased.
- Includes partition-aware flashing, watchdog-reset recovery and exact-version post-flash verification.
- Preserves cadence autotune and calibration-gated detector thresholds.

This prerelease is checksummed but unsigned. It is not approved for OTA, factory onboarding, or automatic production rollout. Production remains on the last dual-attested release.

- Enforces always-on application operation for power-bank deployments.

name: Talos Desktop v2.2.1 — Migration UI + connection diagnostics + LLM onboarding
body:
## Highlights

- **Migration pipeline** end-to-end: drop files / connect SQL / scan LAN → classify → review → commit (all 11 entities, schema-correct, 24h rollback).
- **LLM onboarding card** with visual provider cards (OpenAI / Anthropic / OpenRouter / Ollama / LM Studio), auto-detect Ollama/LM Studio installed models, real round-trip Test button.
- **Connection diagnostics**: Network / Internet / ERP / LLM status strip with re-check + expand-on-fail.
- **RaspPi appliance** scaffolding: backend-config picker, AddTalosBoxScreen, mDNS/BLE pairing.
- **Bundled migrator** (PyInstaller spec + build scripts) — desktop ships its own Python sidecar.

## Install

```sh
brew tap kivanccakmak/talos
brew install --cask talos      # macOS (arm64)
brew install talos             # Linux (arm64)
```

Windows + Linux x86_64 builds deferred this release (require Certum SimplySign session + Docker respectively).

name: Talos Desktop v2.2.0 — Honeywell MPD31D + Bixolon CUPS support
body:
Empirically-verified label printing on Honeywell MPD31D + Bixolon SPP-L310. Bixolon CUPS driver bundled inside the app; Honeywell MPD31D works out of the box via BLE.

## What's new

- **First-run default printer: Honeywell MPD31D** — connects via BLE, prints CPCL out of the box, no driver install needed
- **Bixolon SPP-L310 support** — the macOS + Linux Bixolon CUPS drivers are bundled inside the app; install via native admin-auth prompt with one click
- **Cloud printer preference** — your printer choice syncs across desktop installs + mobile via Convex
- **Server-enforced hardware rules** — no client can save physically impossible combinations (e.g. Bixolon + BLE — the SPP-L310 SKU has no BLE radio)
- **Per-OS transport gating** — UI shows only the transports your platform supports
- **Specific error codes** — failures now surface actionable hints (BT_NOT_PAIRED, NET_REFUSED, PERMISSION_DENIED, etc.)
- **Canonical CPCL/ZPL generator** — single source of truth shared between web, desktop, and mobile apps

## Downloads

| Platform | File | Size |
|---|---|---|
| macOS Apple Silicon | Talos-2.2.0-macos-arm64.dmg | 95 MB |
| Linux x86_64 (AppImage) | Talos-2.2.0-linux-x86_64.AppImage | 104 MB |
| Linux ARM64 (AppImage) | Talos-2.2.0-linux-arm64.AppImage | 104 MB |
| Linux x86_64 (Debian/Ubuntu) | Talos-2.2.0-linux-amd64.deb | 72 MB |
| Linux ARM64 (Debian/Ubuntu) | Talos-2.2.0-linux-arm64.deb | 67 MB |
| Windows x86_64 | Talos-2.2.0-windows-x86_64.exe (signed) | 76 MB |
| Windows ARM64 | Talos-2.2.0-windows-arm64.exe (signed) | 78 MB |

All binaries are code-signed where applicable:
- macOS: unsigned (Gatekeeper may warn on first launch — right-click → Open)
- Windows: signed with SİMKAB ELEKTRİK certificate via Certum SimplySign
- Linux: AppImage / .deb unsigned per convention

## Verified hardware

| Printer | Transport | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Honeywell MPD31D-V (firmware 5.7.8) | BLE via Microchip MLDP | ✅ Verified end-to-end on macOS — prints QR codes |
| Bixolon SPP-L310 | BT Classic via Bixolon CUPS driver | ✅ Driver bundled; install + CUPS path verified |

## Install

**macOS:** Download the DMG → open → drag Talos to Applications. First launch may show Gatekeeper warning.

**Windows:** Download the .exe → run. Signed installer; SmartScreen may still show "Unknown publisher" until enough downloads build reputation.

**Linux (Debian/Ubuntu):**
```bash
sudo dpkg -i Talos-2.2.0-linux-amd64.deb
```

**Linux (other):**
```bash
chmod +x Talos-2.2.0-linux-x86_64.AppImage
./Talos-2.2.0-linux-x86_64.AppImage
```

## First-run printing flow

1. Log in
2. Printer Settings tab → Honeywell MPD31D is selected by default
3. Power on your MPD31D-V → Scan → Connect → Test Print
4. For Bixolon SPP-L310: pick the Bixolon preset → "Install Bixolon Driver" (native admin prompt) → pair printer in system Bluetooth → Print

## Printing guide

See `docs/MPD31D_PRINTING_GUIDE.md` in the source repo for the full empirically-verified guide to printing on the Honeywell MPD31D from macOS, Linux, Windows, iOS, Android, and Web.
